summary: Per-action idempotency token not propagated for chained function/tool calls resulting in duplicate webhook side-effects
description:
Issue summary: Customer observes duplicate downstream webhook side-effects when using a chained function/tool workflow (generate -> parse -> call-outbound-webhook) with client-side retries enabled. Impact: Duplicate charges and duplicated external notifications for a subset of user requests.

Context: ScribeAI uses a multi-step orchestration where the model generates a structured payload, the SDK executes a local handler that calls an external payment webhook, and the customer has configured the SDK to retry on timeouts with per-request idempotency tokens at the top-level. They reported duplicates only when network blips occurred during the tool-call step or during streaming reconnects.

Observed behavior: When the SDK performs an automatic retry of the overall request, the top-level idempotency token is preserved, but the per-action metadata header that the customer's webhook expects (X-Action-Idempotency) is sometimes regenerated by their orchestration layer or dropped during streaming reconnect. The external service receives two distinct idempotency tokens for the same logical action and accepts both, resulting in duplicate side-effects.

Expected behavior: For chained tool/function calls initiated by one SDK request, any per-action idempotency metadata used to deduplicate downstream side-effects should be stable across retries and reconnects, or SDK documentation should clearly state where responsibility lies for preserving per-action nonces across retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a chat session using SDK (python or go) with a handler that invokes an external webhook from within a function/tool call.
2) Configure SDK retry policy: 3 retries on timeout/backoff with exponential backoff; enable streaming with reconnect enabled.
3) Trigger a request that causes the function call to reach out to the external webhook (payment capture endpoint).
4) Simulate a transient network blip: drop connection when function call is in-flight or cause streaming reconnect on the SDK client side.
5) Observe the external webhook receiving two different idempotency headers for what the customer expects to be a single logical action.
logs: 2026-03-09T17:23:12Z request_id=req-3f7a2c stream_conn=conn-990 drop_reason=timeout handler=payment_capture action_nonce=act-9d2a (first attempt)
2026-03-09T17:23:14Z request_id=req-3f7a2c retry=1 stream_conn=conn-991 handler=payment_capture action_nonce=act-7b5f (retry attempt; nonce differs)
Customer-side outbound webhook logs show two POSTs within 2s: X-Action-Idempotency=act-9d2a and X-Action-Idempotency=act-7b5f; both returned 200.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel (reporter): We're seeing duplicated payment captures for ~0.3% of requests when our service has transient network failures. Top-level request idempotency is in place but per-action nonces differ on retry. Can Support advise if SDK should preserve per-action metadata?

2026-03-10 - Jordan Lee (Support): Thanks for the report — we need a minimal repro and logs. Can you attach SDK client logs with request IDs and the handler code that sets the X-Action-Idempotency header?

2026-03-11 - ScribeAI (customer): Attached stripped logs and a simplified python handler that calls requests.post to the payment endpoint. Note: We generate a new action nonce inside the function call code on every handler invocation. We assumed top-level retry would not re-run the handler if the top-level idempotency token matched.

2026-03-12 - Support (Jordan Lee): Reproduced locally with a test harness. Hypothesis: SDK retry triggers re-execution of the function/tool handler in the customer process for some failure modes (stream reconnects), so any per-action nonce generated inside the handler will be different across attempts. We recommend either: a) move nonce generation to before the handler invocation and pass it into the handler so it's stable across retries, or b) have the SDK surface a per-action stable idempotency header when re-invoking handlers during reconnects.

2026-03-13 - Eng (Riley Chen): We've captured pcap and server-side trace for req-3f7a2c. The serving-runtime saw a reconnect and a resumed session that resulted in the handler being invoked twice. The runtime did not attach or require a per-action idempotency token; it treats handlers as user code. Filing an internal task to add a best-effort propagation hook into SDKs.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Duplicate side-effects due to handler re-execution on SDK-initiated retry or streaming resume.
Confirmed by local repro: when handler generates nonce at invocation time, retry paths produce different nonces and downstream systems accept them.
Relevant traces: trace_id=trace-7c2a8 (attached in internal logs), pcap shows streaming reconnect at 17:23:13Z and two handler invocations within 2s window.

SDK behavior: python SDK v0.14.2 and go SDK v0.9.1 re-invoke user handlers when the server signals a resumed request; JS SDK behavior varies by streaming client implementation. Documented behavior is currently vague about per-action nonce responsibilities.
Risk assessment: High for customers that perform side-effectful operations inside handlers (payments, emails). Estimated incidence: <1% of requests but high business impact when it occurs.
Temporary mitigation tested: customer moved action nonce generation to a request-scoped store (generated before calling into the model/function orchestration) and duplicates stopped in repro.
resolution:
Workaround: Customers should generate action-level idempotency nonces outside of the handler invocation so the same nonce is used across retries. Support updated the SDK troubleshooting guide to add a 'per-action nonce' section and example for python/go/js.

Planned product follow-up: Engineering to evaluate adding an optional stable per-action header propagation in SDKs and an explicit note in streaming/reconnect docs. PRs opened for SDK docs + small SDK helper to attach a stable action_nonce across retries.

Status: Waiting for Engineering prioritization for SDK change; customer applied workaround and confirmed no further duplicates in validation tests.
